text:
Raj Patel: console shows a bunch of clients falling back from SSE -> polling yesterday around 03:12 UTC. looks correlated with the surge, but the billing screen counted both streams and poll requests. anyone see why fallback isn't deduping?
Sophia Chen: saw the same. our routing policy should prefer sticky routing to the same edge for resume. if it flips, client times out and triggers fallback.
Emily Ortiz: examples of log lines? i only have aggregated metrics.
Raj Patel: paste from edge logs: 
```
[03:12:03] session_id=abc123 route=us-west-2 -> sticky=false reconnect_delay=180ms status=RESUME_TIMEOUT
[03:12:04] session_id=abc123 fallback=POLLED_POLL start_ts=161x end_ts=161y tokens=0
```
Noah Kim: aha — resume timeout fires after 150ms, then the client does a short-poll; when resume succeeds later we don't cancel the poll billing. double-count.
Sophia Chen: is the client calling resume aggressively or is the server delaying resume-phase ACK? we changed commit routing last week to add route-heat checks. maybe that's introducing jitter.
Emily Ortiz: i replayed a trace: WS reconnect happened at +320ms after the poll started. poll completed with 204 and counted as a full request.
Raj Patel: so two problems: routing jitter causes delayed reconnection; and console/billing pipeline treats poll as a separate charge even if resume later links them. need a fix across stack.
Noah Kim: proposal: extend resume grace window server-side to 500ms for pooled clients, and emit a correlation-id for fallback polls so billing can dedupe if resume occurs within window.
Sophia Chen: sending correlation-id requires client change though. can we do server-side best-effort by mapping session_id -> poll_id when resume happens?
Emily Ortiz: billing team hates heuristics but accepts deterministic keys. correlation-id from server would be deterministic. we could add an optional header `X-Resume-Correlation` on 204 responses.
Raj Patel: timeline? this is causing spikes in unit cost for some tenants. also console UI shows duplicate sessions which confuses SRE.
Noah Kim: short-term: increase resume window to 400ms and emit a console flag `resume_in_flight` so UI hides polls that overlap. medium-term: add correlation-id header and update billing pipeline to dedupe matching session_id + correlation within 1s.
Sophia Chen: agree. i'll prep a canary: runtime change + console toggle, then billing follow-up. canary on canary-dev first.
Emily Ortiz: i'll write the billing PR template. need the exact header name and semantics.
Noah Kim: header: `X-Resume-Correlation: <session_id>-<resume_nonce>` — runtime will generate nonce when a resume attempt is initiated and include it in any fallback response until resume finalizes.
Raj Patel: sounds good. also add telemetry event `resume.fallback.dedupable=true` so we can query how many polls become deduped.
Sophia Chen: noted. i'll drop a patch this afternoon. @deploy-bot can we run a canary rollout to canary-dev with 10% traffic and the `resume_window_ms=400` flag?
deploy-bot: Deploy request received for runtime-service canary-dev with overrides: {"resume_window_ms":400, "emit_resume_header":true} — started canary at 2026-03-20T16:40:00Z :rocket:
Emily Ortiz: i'll coordinate with billing to hold on final dedupe until we have a deterministic header in prod.
Noah Kim: one more UX ask — console should display a single session line and show both 'resume' and 'poll' events in a compact expandable view rather than two separate sessions. reduces ops noise.
Sophia Chen: agree, file a console ticket pls.
Raj Patel: thanks team. i'll monitor cost dashboards and post updates here. :thumbsup:
